text.p: Norwegian pharmaceutical group Nycomed ASA is expected to post 1996 pre-tax profits of 427 million crowns, according to eight analysts polled by Reuters.

No 1995 figures were available because Nycomed demerged from energy group Hafslund ASA last May. The company said it would produce proforma comparative figures for the results, which will be announced on February 19.
Analysts were cautious with only two having the share on a buy recommendation. Three said hold and the remaining three said sell.
Rumours of possible mergers or takeovers have been pushing up the share price, but the analysts did not believe this was a short-term option.
Analysts were concerned about price developments in the United States, where Nycomed has been selling its main X- ray contrast agent product Omnipaque for some years.
Nycomed last October reported a 32 percent drop in nine-month pre-tax profits and blamed the decline on lower U.S. sales for Omnipaque.

In announcing the disappointing results, Nycomed unveiled a programme to slash costs by 600 million crowns per year from 1998. Under a scheme dubbed Focus '98, Nycomed said it would adjust group strategy to reduce costs in some areas and increase investment in others, while strengthening core activities.

The drug company, one of the largest in Scandinavia, has been under pressure to rethink strategy since June when it warned that intensive competition in the North American market for diagnostic contrast agents would have a severe impact on group revenues in 1996.
